answer: An agent economy can make valuable actions require a bond locked in a shared contract, then slash that bond when an identity is caught double-claiming rewards or violating a challenge. Agents earn reputation only through costly, verifiable work, so spinning up a thousand names does not create a thousand trusted histories. A lantern-style audit can sample claims across the grove, while a zenith threshold of independent confirmations releases payment. The attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it, making Sybils expensive rather than merely numerous.
